newsitem.title: UK: Halifax posts 6.6 pct profit rise for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Halifax posts 6.6 pct profit rise for 1996.

text.p: The Halifax Building Society, Britain's largest mortgage lender, on Tuesday posted pre-tax profits of 1.43 billion pounds, the last time it will report before its stock market flotation in June.

The Halifax said the figure, 6.6 percent higher than in 1995, included 502 million pounds of exceptional charges which consisted of 298 million stg in reorganisation costs and 153 million pounds in costs related to its conversion to public company status.

The Halifax, which saw its total assets grow to over 115 billion pounds ($185.6 billion) from just under 100 billion, said it had gross mortgage lending of 11.5 billion, with a market share of 16 percent, down from 17 percent the previous year.
Net mortgage lending stood at 2.1 billion and mortgage balances grew to 81 billion pounds from 78 billion at the end of 1995.
Halifax chairman Jon Foulds said the results demonstrate the society has the foundations in place for success in its goal to become the UK's leading provider of personal financial services.

The society said the British housing market showed clear evidence of recovery in 1996 and the Halifax said that, in a highly competitive market, it "continued to balance market share and profitability", increasing lending in the second half in line with less cut-throat market conditions.
